ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Shoulder and arm trauma foundations: 4

A motorcyclist has a scapular fracture, chest bruising and shortness of breath. The visible shoulder injury does not explain the respiratory findings. Which principle should guide the trauma assessment before focusing on definitive scapular treatment?

  1. Protected early motion when stability permits
  2. Assess associated injuries beyond the visible fracture
  3. Document neurovascular status before and after intervention
  4. CT to define the injury and adjacent structures
  5. Urgent specialist evaluation and controlled treatment
Answer and explanation

Assess associated injuries beyond the visible fracture

High-energy injuries can coexist with chest, neurovascular or adjacent-joint injuries that alter priorities.

Option explanations

Assess associated injuries beyond the visible fracture: High-energy injuries can coexist with chest, neurovascular or adjacent-joint injuries that alter priorities.

Document neurovascular status before and after intervention: Serial motor, sensory and perfusion examinations establish baseline function and detect new deficits after reduction or splinting. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

CT to define the injury and adjacent structures: CT helps evaluate complex bony anatomy, articular involvement or sternoclavicular relationships when indicated. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Urgent specialist evaluation and controlled treatment: Threatened neurovascular or mediastinal structures require urgent appropriately supported care, not casual manipulation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Protected early motion when stability permits: Appropriate early motion reduces stiffness; timing depends on stability and the treatment plan. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
